name: @signal8ai/mcp

tools.name: search_companies
tools.description: Search for companies by name or ticker symbol in the Signal8 database. Returns matching companies with their ticker, name, CIK, and exchange. Use this as the first step to find a company before calling other tools.

query.description: Search query - company name or ticker symbol (e.g., "Tesla", "TSLA")

tools.name: get_company_profile
tools.description: Get an enriched company profile by ticker symbol. Returns CIK, exchange, sector, industry, market cap, employee count, description, and other fundamental data. This is a lightweight lookup -- use this when you only need basic company info rather than the full bundle. Always includes halted/haltCode/haltedAt trading-halt status (false/null when trading normally); a halted-but-listed ticker reports delisted:false. `sharesOutstanding` is DATED: `sharesOutstandingAsOf` + `sharesOutstandingAsOfKind` ("stated" = the issuer's statement date; "checked" = when it was last confirmed against a vendor; "none" = date not recorded) and a vendor-free `sharesOutstandingSource`. Quote the date with the count; null is NOT MEASURED, never zero.

tools.name: get_quote
tools.description: Get the current stock quote for a company including price, volume, change, market cap, and other real-time market data. Use this when a user asks about a stock's current price or trading activity. Always includes halted/haltCode/haltReason/haltedAt/resumptionAt trading-halt fields (false/null when trading normally); a halted ticker returns the last-known quote instead of an error, or currentPrice:null + halted:true when nothing is recoverable. marketCap is the live price × the SEC-derived share count; when that count is unavailable it is null with marketCapWithheldReason set — NOT MEASURED, never "no market cap" and never $0. The count itself rides as `sharesOutstanding` with `sharesOutstandingAsOf` + `sharesOutstandingAsOfKind` ("stated" = the issuer's statement date; "checked" = when it was last confirmed against a vendor; "none" = date not recorded) and a vendor-free `sharesOutstandingSource` — quote the date with the count.

tools.name: get_market_metrics
tools.description: Get computed market metrics for a company including volume averages, volatility, SMAs, and trend direction. Use when analyzing trading patterns or technical indicators beyond the basic quote.

tools.name: get_short_interest
tools.description: Get short interest data for a company including short volume, short ratio, days to cover, and short percent of float. Use when analyzing bearish sentiment or potential short squeeze setups. 🔴 "shortInterestPercent" null ALWAYS carries "shortInterestPercentReason" (since 2026-10-04): "float_not_point" = the float on record is a snapshot BOUND or ESTIMATE (<= / >= / ~), and a percent-of-float is never struck off a bound — do NOT divide "shortInterest" by a ceiling, floor or estimate from get_float yourself; "float_unavailable" = no float of any kind on record; "short_pct_of_float_unreconciled" = a point float existed but the ratio was implausible or the split basis could not be resolved. A null percent is NOT MEASURED, never 0%.

tools.name: get_float
tools.description: Get float data for a company: floatShares, floatDefinition, as-of date, and — when the headline float is WITHHELD — the bounds and labelled stand-ins that replace it. Use when analyzing share supply. The share count the float was judged against (`basisSharesOutstanding`) is DATED: `sharesOutstandingAsOf` + `sharesOutstandingAsOfKind` ("stated" / "checked" / "none" = date not recorded) and a vendor-free `sharesOutstandingSource`; never present the count without its date. CARDINAL RULE: null / absent / withheld means NOT MEASURED — never "no float", never "no restricted shares", never zero. A numeric 0 is a MEASURED zero and passes a null check, so decide from the reason/marker field ("floatWithheldReason", "restrictedBlockCount", "provenance", "direction"), never from the value alone. IMPORTANT: check "floatDefinition" to know which float you are reading — "tradeable" (shares outstanding minus affiliates minus restricted/unregistered blocks: what can actually reach the tape; used on filing-derived dilution-snapshot tickers), "non_affiliate" (the SEC I.B.6 figure, which INCLUDES restricted shares held by non-affiliates — not what a trader means by float), "non_affiliate_estimate" (approximated from ownership filings), or "free_float" (vendor methodology). TODAY "floatDefinition" and "source" are only present on dilution-snapshot results: a vendor-sourced float arrives with neither (just floatShares, asOfDate, floatEstimated) because vendors are not named — read an ABSENT floatDefinition as "not a filing-derived tradeable float" and do not assume it is tradeable. On snapshot tickers "nonAffiliateFloatShares" carries the SEC I.B.6 figure separately — it is the ONLY correct input to baby-shelf / I.B.6 shelf-capacity math; never use the tradeable float there, and never present the non-affiliate figure as tradeable supply. floatShares:null with "floatWithheldReason" set ("restricted_blocks_unnetted" | "stated_figure_impossible" | "affiliate_basis_stale" | "affiliate_figure_declined" | "affiliate_unreconciled" | "share_count_unavailable" | "split_post_dates_basis" | "split_unconfirmed" | "snapshot_float_unconfirmed" | "refusal_evaluation_failed") means the figure was deliberately WITHHELD by the snapshot AND no lower tier could answer — do not substitute a vendor float of your own. Since 2026-09-29 a snapshot that withheld its float FALLS THROUGH: when a lower tier can answer, "source" names that tier (computed / sec-10k / polygon / fmp), "floatShares" is ITS figure under ITS definition, and "snapshotFloatWithheldReason" carries the snapshot's reason as context ("the filing-derived snapshot could not state a float; showing <source>"). Read that field as provenance, never as a second refusal. 🔴 SINCE 2026-10-03 THE SNAPSHOT FIGURE ALWAYS HEADLINES: when the snapshot carries ANY figure — "floatEstimate" (~ point / <= ceiling / >= floor), "tradeableFloatCeiling", or an "affiliateBasis" range — "floatShares" stays null and THAT figure is the answer, with its label; a lower tier that also answered and passed the guard rides "otherSourceFloat" {floatShares, source, provenance:"other_source", floatDefinition, asOfDate} as a SECONDARY "other source" line — never the float, never arithmetic. A lower tier fills "floatShares" ONLY when the snapshot carries no figure at all. 🔴 SINCE 2026-10-04 A TRIVIAL CEILING IS NOT A FIGURE: a snapshot ceiling ("tradeableFloatCeiling", a "floatEstimate" with bound "ceiling", or an upper-only "affiliateBasis" range) at or above 99% of the share count says only "the float is at most every issued share" and is STRIPPED from the response (null), so the lower tier may headline under its own "source" with "snapshotFloatWithheldReason" as context (GELS: Polygon 5.12M, not "<= 11.18M" on 11.18M shares). Floors and point estimates are never stripped. EXCEPT (2026-10-08): a "floatEstimate" with rung "affiliate_sizing_estimate" carries a "reason" built from the filings' itemised insiders (e.g. "no reported insider holdings (4 affiliates at zero); 1 unreported: <name> (CFO, since <date>)") and "unsizedAffiliates" [{holder, role, since}]; it is KEPT even at the share count because the reason is a finding — quote the reason with the figure, and never present it as floatShares. A "shares_outstanding_ceiling" whose "reason" states a declared affiliate floor ("the insider holdings the filings size total at least N shares") may likewise be served at the share count, but ONLY as the last resort when no lower tier answered or its answer was refused (2026-10-11). 🔴 SUPERSEDED LATER ON 2026-10-11: EVERY "shares_outstanding_ceiling" now carries a "reason" (the declared floor, or "the filings do not size the insider holdings, so none are deducted") and HEADLINES even at the share count — a vendor figure then rides "otherSourceFloat" only. A "floatEstimate" may also carry "qualifier" (a short label — quote it with the figure, e.g. "insider holdings not sized") and "offBasis" (an array): "pre_split_as_filed" = the figure is AS OF "asOf", BEFORE the split(s) in "splitsAfter" [{ratio, effectiveDate, status}], NOT restated across them; "ordinary_shares_unconverted" = in ORDINARY shares on an ADS whose ratio is unresolved, NOT ADSs; "count_predates_issuances" = struck from a dated filing-cover count ("countSource") with later issuances not counted. An "offBasis" figure is true ONLY with its label: never compare it with a price, a market cap, another float or a threshold, and never state it without the label. Since 2026-10-01 that fall-through is GUARDED: a lower-tier figure dated before a split the snapshot names, or outside the snapshot's own floor / ceiling / point estimate, or (since 2026-10-08) COUNTED before share issuances the snapshot records totalling at least 10% of it, is REFUSED and the withheld envelope is served with "fallbackRefusal" {reason: "fallback_predates_split" | "fallback_predates_issuance" | "fallback_outside_snapshot_bounds", refusedSource, detail} beside the snapshot's "floatWithheldReason". The refused figure is NOT in the response and must not be fetched from a vendor to fill the gap — the detail says why no lower tier is shown either. A snapshot that stated a float never carries it. A withheld result may carry up to four stand-ins, each labelled IN the object; NONE is a float and NONE may be fed to a market cap, a percent-of-float, a short-interest ratio, a screen, a sort or a comparison: (1) "tradeableFloatCeiling" is an UPPER BOUND — the tradeable float is AT MOST this; render it with "<=" and nothing else (null = no bound stateable, never 0). (2) "affiliateBasis.floatLowerBound" / "floatUpperBound" are a RANGE the float lies in — "between X and Y"; each end is null independently when not measurable, so state the ends that exist as inequalities. They bound the NON-AFFILIATE float, which still INCLUDES restricted shares held by non-affiliates — NOT the tradeable floatShares. This object also appears on PUBLISHED floats; there it is context, never a bound on floatShares (a "convention_conservative" tradeable figure can sit BELOW floatLowerBound because it also deducts the restricted shares the bound includes — that is not a contradiction). (3) "floatEstimate" is a BADGED ESTIMATE {shares, basis, direction, confidence}: "basis" is the itemised working (quote it), "direction" says which way it errs ("overstates" = the true float is at most shares; "understates" = at least; "unknown"), "confidence" describes the estimate, not a float. Since 2026-09-29 it is the SNAPSHOT FLOAT LADDER figure on any withheld snapshot ticker and may also carry "rung" ("non_affiliate_estimate" | "shares_outstanding_ceiling" | "rolled_forward_lower_bound" | "recital_rolled_forward_estimate" | "successor_exchange_estimate" | "affiliate_sizing_estimate" | "restricted_block_ceiling" — at most O/S less affiliates, less the restricted blocks the filings place outside them and the part of the unplaced blocks too large to fit inside them), "bound" ("point" = about X, render "~X"; "ceiling" = AT MOST X, render "<= X"; "floor" = AT LEAST X, render ">= X") and "asOf"; a floor or ceiling is a BOUND, never a point value. null means no figure could be derived from the snapshot's structured fields. An estimate never becomes floatShares — present shares WITH basis and direction, never alone. Unrelated to the boolean "floatEstimated", which flags a published floatShares back-derived from a USD public-float disclosure. (4) "vendorFallback" is a third-party free-float figure {floatShares, provenance:"vendor", floatDefinition:"free_float", asOfDate, splitAdjusted} offered beside the withhold — NOT our number, NOT on the tradeable definition, already refused when our filings refute it. Present it as the vendor free float as of its own date, never in the "Float" slot. "restrictedShares":null means NOT MEASURED (a block exists whose size the filings do not state), NEVER zero; "restrictedBlockCount":0 is an answer, not an absence. "affiliateBasisStale" (with basisSpanDays/affiliateAnchorDate) labels a float whose affiliate table is materially older than its share count — the number itself is unchanged. "tradeableBasis":"convention_conservative" means the filings did not answer and a published convention resolved it — see "tradeableConvention" and do not present the figure as exact.

tools.name: get_float_history
tools.description: Get the POINT-IN-TIME float history for a company — one sample per trade date (float shares, shares outstanding, and the source the float came from). Use to answer "what was the float on date X" or to see float expand across a dilution event, which the latest-only get_float cannot show. IMPORTANT: this series is FORWARD-ONLY — it began accumulating in mid-2026 and is NOT backfilled, so early/absent history is expected and an empty rows array is a normal result, not an error or a delisted company. Each row carries "source" ("polygon" | "computed" | "sec_10k" | "fmp") because float quality varies by provider — weigh rows accordingly rather than treating all sources as equal. Charged per your API tier.

days.description: Lookback window in trade dates. Default 90, clamped to 1-730.

tools.name: get_historical_prices
tools.description: Get historical OHLCV price candles for a stock. Supports daily, weekly, and monthly resolutions. Use period shorthand (1M, 3M, 6M, 1Y, 5Y, ALL) or explicit from/to UNIX timestamps. Default is 1 year of daily candles. Use this to compute price returns, chart price history, or analyze volume trends over time.

period.description: Lookback period shorthand (default: "1Y"). Ignored if from/to are provided.

from.description: Start date as UNIX timestamp (overrides period)

to.description: End date as UNIX timestamp (overrides period)

tools.name: get_stock_price_change
tools.description: Get percentage price changes for a stock across multiple timeframes: 1D, 5D, 1M, 3M, 6M, YTD, 1Y, 3Y, 5Y, 10Y, and MAX. Use this for quick "how much is it up/down" answers without fetching full candle data.

tools.name: get_financials
tools.description: Get income statement, balance sheet, and cash flow data for a company. Supports annual, quarterly, and trailing-twelve-month views. Use when analyzing revenue, profitability, debt, or cash position.

type.description: Financial period type: "annual", "quarter", or "ttm" (trailing twelve months). Defaults to annual.

limit.description: Maximum number of periods to return (1-40). Defaults to 8.

tools.name: get_earnings
tools.description: Get historical earnings data for a company including EPS actual vs estimate, revenue actual vs estimate, and surprise percentages. Use when analyzing earnings beats/misses or upcoming earnings expectations.

limit.description: Maximum number of earnings periods to return (1-40). Defaults to 8.

tools.name: get_executives
tools.description: Get key executives and officers of a company including name, title, compensation, and tenure. Use when researching company leadership or management quality.

tools.name: get_news
tools.description: Get recent news articles and press releases for a company. Use when researching recent developments, catalysts, or sentiment drivers. Set pressReleasesOnly to return only official company press releases.

limit.description: Maximum number of articles to return (1-20). Defaults to 10.

pressReleasesOnly.description: When true, return only official company press releases (exclude third-party news).

tools.name: get_analyst_consensus
tools.description: Get analyst ratings consensus for a company including average target price, number of analysts, buy/hold/sell breakdown, and consensus recommendation. Use when evaluating Wall Street sentiment or price targets.

tools.name: get_analyst_estimates
tools.description: Get forward analyst estimates for a company including EPS, revenue, EBITDA, and net income (low/high/avg) with analyst counts. Supports annual and quarterly periods. Use when analyzing forward earnings expectations or revenue forecasts.

limit.description: Maximum number of estimate periods to return (1-40). Defaults to 8.

tools.name: get_clinical_trials
tools.description: Get clinical trial data for a biotech/pharma company including trial phase, status, conditions, and interventions. Use when analyzing a biotech company's pipeline or upcoming catalyst events.

limit.description: Maximum number of clinical trials to return (1-50). Defaults to 10.

tools.name: search_clinical_trials
tools.description: Search clinical trials market-wide (cross-company). Distinct from get_clinical_trials, which is scoped to a single ticker. Filter by phase, indication, sponsor, status, and date window; sort and paginate the results.

tools.name: get_top_movers
tools.description: Top stock movers — gainers (largest % up), losers (largest % down), or active (highest volume). Optional session window (premarket / regular / afterhours; regular default; not supported for active). Optional date (YYYY-MM-DD) returns a PAST trade date's gainers/losers on a historical daily close-to-close basis (computed from split-adjusted daily bars, NOT intraday) — session is rejected when date is set, date is not supported for direction=active, and a non-trade date (weekend/holiday) returns an empty list (not an error). Penny-stock artifacts are filtered by default — set includePennyStocks to include sub-$1 movers.

direction.description: Mover direction: gainers, losers, or active (volume)

limit.description: Optional max rows (1–100). Backend default applied when omitted.

session.description: Session window: premarket (4:00–9:30 AM ET), regular (RTH close-to-close, default), afterhours (4:00–8:00 PM ET). Live-only — rejected (400) when combined with date.

includePennyStocks.description: Loosen penny-stock artifact guards. Default false enforces prev_close >= $1 and a $1M dollar-volume floor. Set true to allow sub-$1 movers (prev_close >= $0.10, no dollar-volume floor). The ABS(change_pct) <= 500 cap applies in both modes.

date.description: Optional past trade date (YYYY-MM-DD). When set, returns that day's top gainers/losers computed on a historical daily close-to-close basis from split-adjusted daily bars (NOT intraday, NOT session-specific). Rejected with 400 when combined with a non-regular session or with direction="active"; a future or malformed date is also 400. A weekend/holiday date returns an empty list, not an error.

tools.name: get_market_news
tools.description: Get the latest market-wide news across ALL tickers, most recent first. Every item is significance-classified at ingest (critical | major | standard); the default filter of critical,major is the "top stories" view. Use for "what is happening in the market right now" — for news about one company, use get_news with a ticker instead. Requires the /news/latest public endpoint (added 2026-07-29; 404 until that backend deploy).

limit.description: Maximum items to return (1-50). Defaults to 10.

significance.description: CSV of levels to include, e.g. "critical,major" (default) or "critical,major,standard".

tools.name: get_market_breadth
tools.description: Get market breadth aggregates (advance/decline counts and ratio, percent of constituents above their 50DMA and 200DMA, and counts of new 52-week highs/lows) for a chosen universe (sp500, ndx, or all). Use to add market-state context to commentary, tweets, or daily summaries.

universe.description: Universe to aggregate over: sp500, ndx, or all (default sp500)

tools.name: get_trading_halts
tools.description: List currently-active trading halts across NASDAQ/NYSE/AMEX (from the consolidated Nasdaq Trader halt feed). Each halt includes ticker, market, haltCode (T1/T2/T12/LUDP/H10/...), human-readable reason, haltedAt, and the scheduled resumptionAt when one is set. An EMPTY list is a normal state (no active halts right now), not an error. Halts are tradeable catalysts — use this to discover halted names, then get_quote for the frozen last price.

tools.name: get_earnings_calendar
tools.description: Get upcoming and recent earnings releases between two dates. Optionally restrict to a list of tickers. Returns ticker, date, time (BMO/AMC), EPS estimate, and revenue estimate when available. Supports market cap filtering to focus on large-cap or small-cap earnings only.

minMarketCap.description: Minimum market cap in USD (e.g., 10000000000 for $10B+)

maxMarketCap.description: Maximum market cap in USD (e.g., 2000000000 for under $2B)

tools.name: get_economic_calendar
tools.description: Get scheduled macro/economic events (CPI, FOMC, jobs reports, GDP, etc.) between two dates. Optionally filter to a single country (ISO-3166 alpha-2, e.g. "US"). Defaults to US when omitted.

tools.name: get_filing_calendar
tools.description: Get the forward-looking 10-K / 10-Q SEC filing-deadline calendar within a date window. Optionally restrict to a universe (sp500/ndx/dji/all) and/or a list of form types (default both 10-K and 10-Q).

formTypes.description: Optional SEC form types subset, e.g. ["10-Q"]

tools.name: get_post_earnings_movers
tools.description: Get stocks that moved significantly after earnings reports on a given date. Returns pre-computed price changes with earnings surprise data in a single call — no need to chain get_earnings_calendar + get_historical_prices + get_quote per ticker. Includes preEarningsClose, currentPrice, changePct, EPS/revenue actuals vs estimates, and surprise percentages. Filter by minimum absolute % change threshold.

minChangePct.description: Minimum absolute % price change to include (default 5). Set to 0 for all.

tools.name: get_recent_material_filings
tools.description: Recent material 8-K filings (last 7 days) for the constituents of an index universe. By default returns the high-signal 8-K item codes (material agreements, M&A, executive changes, restructurings, etc.); pass `items` to filter to specific 8-K item codes. Choose the universe with `universe`.

universe.description: Index universe to scan (sp500, ndx, or dji).

tools.name: screen_sec_filings
tools.description: Screen SEC filings across all companies with company-level filters (sector, industry, market cap, exchange) combined with filing-level filters (form type, date range). Returns filings enriched with company metadata: ticker, sector, industry, exchange, market cap, and price. Use this to answer questions like "find all S-1 filings from biotech companies under $500M market cap" or "show me recent 8-K filings from Technology sector companies". This is the most powerful filing DISCOVERY tool for filings — use search_sec_filings only when you already know the specific CIK. This tool returns FILINGS, not a company universe: to enumerate or COUNT companies by market cap / price / float (e.g. "find all companies under $300M market cap"), use screen_companies instead — it supports minMarketCapComputed / maxMarketCapComputed and returns a real total COUNT. Searches only the 500 largest matching companies by market cap (narrow the filters to reach smaller ones); for float, price, company-type, foreign-issuer or recent-IPO filters, full-text queries, or 8-K item codes, use search_sec_filings with its company filters. Coverage: Signal8's archive of SEC EDGAR filings in the archive's held range (see `archiveFrom` in each response; currently from late 2021, expanding back to 2016 as the history backfill fills in), updated through the day. The archive only holds filings from its `archiveFrom` date; before that it holds only a scatter (well under 1% of most years), so ABSENCE BEFORE archiveFrom IS NOT EVIDENCE a filing was never filed — check SEC EDGAR for earlier periods. Some rows are record-only (bodyStored: false — metadata from the EDGAR index with no document body), so their text cannot be read here; open them at their sec.gov URL.

industry.description: Filter by industry (e.g., "Biotechnology", "Software - Application", "Oil & Gas E&P")

minMarketCap.description: Minimum market cap in USD (e.g., 1000000000 for $1B)

maxMarketCap.description: Maximum market cap in USD (e.g., 500000000 for $500M)

sortBy.description: Sort results by field (default: filing_date). Ties are broken by filing id, so a given page is stable and reproducible for a fixed corpus.

sortOrder.description: Sort direction (default: desc). Note that paging is offset-based over a corpus that is continuously ingesting new filings, so when walking many pages of a broad date range, newly-arrived filings can shift rows between pages; page on a closed dateFrom/dateTo window if you need an exhaustive, non-overlapping traversal.

tools.name: search_sec_filings
tools.description: Search and list SEC filings by company (CIK), form type, date range, 8-K item codes and excluded forms, optionally with a full-text query over filing bodies, and optionally by COMPANY FACTS (market cap, float, price, sector, industry, exchange, company type, foreign issuer, recent IPO). Returns rows with `id` (the filingId for get_filing_document / get_filing_exhibits), cik, company_name, accession_number, form_type, filing_date, acceptedAt, primaryDocument, bodyStored and itemNumbers, plus `pagination` with `total`, `totalRelation` ("eq" exact; "gte" a lower bound when the count was cut at 10,000 — then `totalEstimate`, when present, is "about N"), `hasMore` and `nextCursor`. With `q`, unfiltered rows also carry `rank` and a `snippet`. Coverage: Signal8's archive of SEC EDGAR filings in the archive's held range (see `archiveFrom` in each response; currently from late 2021, expanding back to 2016 as the history backfill fills in), updated through the day. The archive only holds filings from its `archiveFrom` date; before that it holds only a scatter (well under 1% of most years), so ABSENCE BEFORE archiveFrom IS NOT EVIDENCE a filing was never filed — check SEC EDGAR for earlier periods. Some rows are record-only (bodyStored: false — metadata from the EDGAR index with no document body), so their text cannot be read here; open them at their sec.gov URL. Full-text `q`: Query syntax: unquoted words must ALL appear (any order, any distance); "quoted phrase" = exact wording; OR between alternatives (merger OR acquisition); -word or -"phrase" to exclude; w1 NEAR/10 w2 (also NEAR(10), or bare NEAR = within 10) = words close together; word* = prefix of 4+ letters (dilut* matches dilution, dilutive); $AAPL or a capitalised ticker scopes to that company; a form code (8-K, 10-Q, S-1), "item 5.02" / "8-K 1.05" and a bare year (2024) scope to that form / 8-K item / year. The archive's reading of the query (tickers/companies, forms, items, years, synonym expansions such as buyback → share repurchase) is returned in `meta.understanding` when stated; pass understand=false to search the words literally. Pass facets=true for `facets` — counts of matching filings per form type, per year and per 8-K item over the WHOLE result set (absent when not measured, e.g. on the Postgres engine — never read absence as zero). With sort=relevance, page 1 shows at most a few filings per company; meta.diversity { maxPerCompany, hidden: [{cik, count}] } names who has more — page on with nextCursor (not page) or filter by that CIK. SECTION SEARCH: section=risk_factors (or mdna, business, ex99 for press releases, item_5_02, …) restricts matching to those sections; rows then carry matchedSections and meta.sections confirms it — if meta.unsupported names section instead, the whole filing was searched. exhibitTypes=EX-10 keeps filings with a material contract (EX-99.1 press release, EX-97 clawback, …); facets=true adds facets.sections / facets.exhibitTypes when measured. An empty text result is only definitive when the response's `searchIndex.complete` is true — otherwise `notes` says the index has not confirmed full coverage of the range. Every response carries `archiveFrom` and `rangeStartsBeforeArchive`: a range with no dateFrom, or starting before archiveFrom, is NEVER definitive (`searchIndex.complete: false`, `reason: "outside_held_range"`, `heldFrom`) and `notes` says so — report "the archive only holds filings from <archiveFrom>; absence before that is not evidence", never "no such filing exists". Pass a dateFrom on or after archiveFrom for a definitive empty answer. The `ciks` filter matches the filing's own CIK: an insider Form 4 filed under the reporting owner's CIK is NOT returned for the issuer's CIK. COMPANY FILTERS (any of minMarketCap … recentIpo) are served from the archive only, using Signal8's company data: (1) only issuer-filed forms are searched (10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, S-1, S-3, 424B*, DEF 14A, 20-F, 6-K, …); third-party forms such as Form 4, 144 and SCHEDULE 13D/G are dropped and listed in `companyFilter.droppedForms` — unless `companyFilter.subjectMatch` is true, in which case they ARE searched, matched by the company they are about — and with no formTypes the default is 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, S-1, S-3, DEF 14A, 20-F, 40-F, 6-K; (2) companies with no measured value for a filter are EXCLUDED, never assumed, and `companyFilter.unknown` counts them per filter; (3) unknown values (e.g. a misspelt sector) are a 400 that lists the allowed names; (4) when the archive cannot answer (e.g. a date range it does not fully hold yet) the call FAILS with code COMPANY_FILTER_NOT_APPLIED and a reason — it never returns unfiltered rows; (5) results are cursor-paged (use nextCursor, not page) and cannot be combined with acceptedFrom/acceptedTo/bodyStored; company-filtered text matches carry no snippet (use search_filing_text with the accessionNumber for the excerpt). The response then includes `companyFilter` (matchedCompanies, searchedCompanies, unknown, forms, droppedForms), `appliedFilters` and `notes`. To COUNT or list companies (not filings) by market cap etc., use screen_companies instead.

ciks.description: Comma-separated CIK numbers to filter by (e.g., "320193,1018724"; zero-padded also accepted)

q.description: Full-text query over filing bodies. Each insider includes a transactionBreakdown by SEC code (P=Purchase, S=Sale, F=Tax withholding, M=Exercise, G=Gift, A=Award), netSharesSold12m (code S only, excludes tax withholding), and isPrimarilyTaxWithholding flag to distinguish routine RSU vesting from discretionary selling. tools.name: get_ownership
tools.description: Get unified ownership breakdown for a company combining Form 4 insider holdings, 13F institutional holdings, and 13D/13G activist positions. All entities are resolved across the three SEC form types into a single view with counterparty resolution. The allHolders array is paginated via limit/offset (default 100). Aggregate stats (institutional/insider/beneficial totals and percentages, plus the `retail` residual) are always included in full. `retail` is the UNATTRIBUTED residual: shares no filing accounts for, which includes recent offering buyers and acquisition holders who have not filed as well as retail investors — an upper bound on retail, never a retail count. When `retail.reason` is `filed_exceeds_outstanding` the residual is withheld (null) because the counted filings exceed the shares outstanding. 🔴 A bucket (`institutional` / `insider` / `beneficial`) whose shares exceed the shares outstanding by more than a 2% timing tolerance has its `percentOfOutstanding` WITHHELD — null, with `percentWithheldReason: "ownership_exceeds_outstanding"` — and its `totalShares` still published: the percent would not be a measurement (filings on another share basis such as ordinary shares against an ADS count, another class reported under this one, shares lent and reported by both lender and buyer, or filings dated before a buyback or redemption). Report the share figure and the reason; NEVER present such a bucket as 100%, as 0%, or as any percent. When any bucket is withheld, `retail.reason` is `ownership_exceeds_outstanding` and `filedSumPercent` is absent. A null percent with NO `percentWithheldReason` means no share count was available — not measured for a different reason. `sharesOutstanding` is the denominator of every percentage and is DATED: `sharesOutstandingAsOf` + `sharesOutstandingAsOfKind` ("stated" = the issuer's statement date; "checked" = when the figure was last confirmed against a vendor; "none" = date not recorded) and `sharesOutstandingSource` (a vendor-free label). Never present a count without its date. `beneficial.staleShares` / `stalePercentOfOutstanding` / `staleHolderCount` is a MEASURED SUBSET of the counted 5%+ total resting on 13D/G schedules >= 24 months old with no newer reaffirming filing by the same holder family — not a deduction; the total still includes it. A row's `reaffirmedBy` names the newer family filing; `staleFiling.ageMonths` marks a counted row with none. `stalePercentOfOutstanding: null` is not measurable (no share count), never zero.

tools.name: screen_companies
tools.description: Since 2026-10-03 the float column ALWAYS carries the dilution snapshot's own figure when the snapshot has one: "float" is the measured POINT float (null on a withheld snapshot row), and such a row then carries "floatEstimate" (shares) + "floatEstimateBound" ("point" ~ / "ceiling" <= / "floor" >=) + "floatEstimateBasis" (the working) — present it as the number with its marker, e.g. "<= 7,953,957". minFloat / maxFloat and the computed_float sort compare the figure's VALUE (COALESCE of the two), so a bounded row is kept; a row with neither is NOT MEASURED, never 0. 🔴 Never feed floatEstimate into a market cap, a percent-of-float or a short-interest ratio — a bound is not a point. Each row carries dividendYield (trailing-twelve-month cash dividends with an ex-date in the last 365 days / current price, in percent), nextExDate and lastExDate — null means NOT MEASURED or not a payer, never 0%. tools.name: get_premarket_scan_history
tools.description: Historical MARKET-WIDE premarket scan for a single PAST trade date. For the requested ET date, returns every ticker with that day's premarket (default) session volume and its relative volume (RVOL) vs the trailing 30-day same-session baseline — the SAME RVOL math as get_rvol_history, but across the whole market for one date instead of one ticker across many dates. Filter by RVOL, market cap, price, and float to backtest screens like "sub-$500M tickers with premarket RVOL > 5 on 2026-07-20" in one call. Rows are ranked by RVOL descending. A future or non-trading date returns an empty list with an explanatory reason (not an error). Every row also reports "baselineState" (why its RVOL is or is not null), "advRatio" (volume ÷ trailing 30-session average FULL-DAY volume) and "advDays"; set includeNoHistory=true to surface high-volume tickers that have no computable RVOL at all, such as first-session new listings. Each row ALSO publishes the RVOL denominator itself as "baselineVolume" (shares) plus a "baselineThin" flag (true when that denominator is under 200 shares): a 90x RVOL off a 1-share baseline is arithmetically correct and analytically worthless. That is almost entirely an asOfTime-basis effect (0.1% of full-session rows vs ~38% at the 04:30 cutoff, falling to ~9% by 09:15) and it skews to LIQUID LARGE CAPS that simply do not trade early, NOT to microcaps. Screen it out with minBaselineVolume and/or minSessionVolume. The response "meta" also reports asOfApplied / asOfIgnored / asOfIgnoredReason, so a time-of-day request that could not be honoured is visible instead of quietly returning full-session numbers. A price / market-cap / float filter can only be applied to a ticker company_screener_data holds a value for, so a just-renamed or just-listed symbol cannot be rated against it. Those rows are NEVER silently dropped: "meta.unscreened" always reports their count, the filter families involved and the tickers, and includeUnscreened=true returns them in "rows" tagged with "unscreenedFilters". Treat that tag as NOT MEASURED — the value is unknown, not out of range. Charged per your API tier.

date.description: REQUIRED past ET trade date to scan (YYYY-MM-DD). Future/non-trade dates return an empty list.

session.description: Session bucket to scan (default premarket). "all" = full extended day.

minRvol.description: Minimum RVOL (day session volume ÷ trailing 30-day baseline). Drops rows whose baseline is not yet warm.

includeNoHistory.description: Also return the cohort minRvol structurally hides: tickers with NO computable RVOL. Two kinds, told apart by each row's "baselineState" — "no-history" (a new listing with no prior trading history at all, so RVOL is meaningless rather than merely missing; e.g. a stock that printed 20M shares on its first-ever session) and "no-cutoff-history" (an established ticker that simply never traded at this cutoff before — a genuine wake-up). Both come back with rvol=null and are ALWAYS ranked BELOW every real-RVOL row, ordered among themselves by "advRatio". Use "advRatio" (volume ÷ trailing 30-session average FULL-DAY volume, null when no full-day denominator exists) and "advDays" (its sample size) to size them — it is NOT an RVOL and is not comparable to one. Inert unless minRvol is set. Default false.

minMarketCap.description: Minimum market cap in USD (market_cap_computed = price × shares outstanding).

maxMarketCap.description: Maximum market cap in USD (e.g. 500000000 for sub-$500M).

minBaselineVolume.description: Minimum RVOL DENOMINATOR in shares. Drops rows whose "baselineVolume" is below it, plus every row that has no baseline at all. This is the direct fix for a huge RVOL computed against a near-zero baseline (e.g. 102 shares ÷ a 1.2-share baseline = 87x on a $10B company that just does not trade at 04:30). Try 200 to match the "baselineThin" flag, or higher for a stricter screen. Does NOT change any RVOL — it only removes rows. Note it also excludes the includeNoHistory cohort, which by definition has no denominator.

minSessionVolume.description: Minimum RVOL NUMERATOR in shares — the scanned session's own volume. Answers "did enough actually trade to be worth acting on?", where minBaselineVolume answers "is the comparison meaningful at all?". USE BOTH IF YOU MEAN BOTH: neither subsumes the other (a 1,000-share floor here cuts thin-baseline rows from ~26% to ~3%, yet a name with an 860-share baseline and 11.8M shares traded passes this and fails a baseline floor).

includeUnscreened.description: Also return rows that could not be RATED against the price / market-cap / float bounds above, because company_screener_data holds no value for them — typically a symbol renamed or listed within the last day (the source is an FMP screener that lags a rename by ~a day). Each such row carries "unscreenedFilters" naming the families that could not be applied, and the matching value field is null. READ THAT AS NOT MEASURED — never as "matched" or "did not match". Default false, in which case those rows are excluded from "rows" but are STILL reported in meta.unscreened (count / columns / tickers), so they are never silently dropped. Inert unless a price, market-cap or float filter is supplied.

limit.description: Max rows to return (1–200, default 50). Rows are ranked by RVOL desc.

asOfTime.description: Optional TRUE time-of-day premarket basis. Any HH:MM ET premarket time; snapped to the nearest 15-minute grid cutoff (04:00–09:15, ties resolve to the earlier cutoff). When set, RVOL is cumulative premarket volume known BY that cutoff ÷ the trailing baselineDays (default 30) average of the SAME cutoff — a real time-of-day comparison, not the full 04:00–09:30 session. Each returned row carries a "basis" field: "asof-0700" (the snapped cutoff actually used) when a precomputed row exists, else "full-session" (automatic per-row fallback — the as-of series is forward-looking and may be sparse). Only applies to a premarket scan. Omit for full-session premarket volume. CHECK "meta.asOfApplied" (the SNAPPED cutoff actually used, or null) and "meta.asOfIgnored" / "meta.asOfIgnoredReason" ("date-not-covered" — the as-of grid has not been computed for this date, so the numbers are full-session; "non-premarket-session" — asOfTime only applies to a premarket scan; "unparseable"). Coverage is a set with HOLES that grows as the backfill runs, so do NOT assume any cutover date — read the meta per request. An unhonoured asOfTime is never an error, so this is the only reliable check. ALSO NOTE: this basis is where near-zero RVOL baselines come from — pair it with minBaselineVolume (see "baselineThin").

baselineDays.description: Rolling RVOL baseline window, in trading rows (same-session days). Default 30; values outside 20-250 are clamped. This is the DENOMINATOR window: every RVOL in the response is that period's volume divided by the average of the trailing N same-session (or same-cutoff) days, excluding the day itself. A SHORTER window tracks recent regime changes faster and is noisier; a LONGER one is smoother and slower to react. The warm-up lookback scales with it automatically, so a wide window is never under-filled into an inflated ratio; the minimum-warm-days gate (20 prior sessions) does NOT scale down, so at the 30-row default a ticker needs 20 of its last 30 sessions populated before rvol is non-null. Omit for the standard 30-day baseline; pass 90 for the pre-2026-09 window.

tools.name: get_politician_disclosures
tools.description: Per-DISCLOSURE feed of politician trades: one item per congressional STOCK Act periodic transaction report (PTR) or executive-branch OGE Form 278-T that contains at least one trade whose bracket LOWER bound is >= minAmount. Works for Congress (sen-/rep-) AND executive branch (exec-) officials. P&L uses price-adjusted share estimation: disclosed amount ranges → estimated shares via historical price → FIFO on shares → open positions marked to current price. tools.name: get_politician_scorecard
tools.description: Top 5 and bottom 5 politicians (Congress + executive-branch officials) by ESTIMATED trading P&L over a trailing window (default and only supported window: 90 days), plus SPY's return over the same window as a benchmark, and imageUrl — a ready-to-attach 2160x2700 PNG card of the same ranking (null when unavailable; card.reason says why). ALL P&L FIGURES ARE ESTIMATES (estimate: true, estimateRange "±25–40%"): disclosed amount RANGES are converted to shares at the historical close, FIFO-matched, and open positions marked to the latest quote. State that they are estimates whenever you publish them; the card already prints "Estimates from disclosed amount ranges (±25–40%). Not investment advice." WHAT THE METRIC IS (read `metric`): P&L on trades DISCLOSED INSIDE the window only — realized on round trips opened and closed in the window plus unrealized on positions opened in the window. It is NOT lifetime P&L; sales of positions bought before the window are not counted. Eligibility: at least 5 trades in the window (eligibility.minTradesInWindow), so a single lucky trade cannot top the board. Each row: slug, fullTitle ("Senator", "Representative", or an executive official's filed title), fullName, displayName, party and state as full words, estimatedPnl, winRate (0-1; null = no position closed in the window — not measured, never 0%), tradesInWindow, unrealizedMeasured, and portraitUrl (always null for executive officials). tools.name: get_dilution_coverage
tools.description: Cheap pre-check for whether Signal8 holds a dilution analysis for a company: coverage status (verified / stale / not_covered), extraction state (never_extracted / running / failed / timeout / complete), last attempt and last success timestamps, the coverage tier, and whether the ticker is out of scope. Never report a company as having no dilution on the strength of an unavailable response. An `outOfScope` ticker is a statement about the PRODUCT (dilution analysis covers small-cap issuers only) and says NOTHING about that company's dilution — do not report a large-cap as having no dilution because it is out of scope. A `stale` status means the analysis is real but predates recent filings. `statusDetail` refines it: `newer_filing_unread` (a material filing — new/amended instrument, 424B5 pricing, split, 10-K — was filed after the snapshot and it has not read it; `unreadFilings` names them) and `delisting_filed` (a Form 25/25-NSE/15 filed after the snapshot; `delistingFiled` names it) both report `status: stale` — say the analysis predates that filing, never present it as current. A null `unreadFilings` is NOT MEASURED, never "nothing filed since". NULL, absent or withheld means NOT MEASURED — it NEVER means "no dilution", "no warrants", "no shelf" or zero. A numeric 0 is a MEASURED zero and defeats a null check, so decide from the accompanying availability/withheld/reason field, never from the value itself. If a figure is absent, say it was not measured; do not describe the company as having none of that instrument. tools.name: get_dilution_risk
tools.description: Get the dilution pressure score: a 0-100 score with its seven-component breakdown (shelf capacity, ATM/equity-line capacity, warrants in the money, convertible proximity, cash burn urgency, historical dilution, toxic financing), plus four risk levels — overall, offering ability, overhead supply, cash need. 🔴 THE SCORE IS MEANINGLESS WITHOUT `scoreMaxMeasured` AND `scoreWithheldReason`: components whose inputs could not be measured are DROPPED FROM THE DENOMINATOR, so a score of 58 may be 58 out of 85, not out of 100. Always report it as `score`/`scoreMaxMeasured` and name the excluded components from `scoreUnmeasuredComponents`; NEVER rescale it to /100, and never treat a low numerator as a low-risk finding. When `scoreDenominatorThin` is true the score rests on fewer than 70 measured points — report it as a PARTIAL reading ("N of M measured"), never as a full one. A non-null `scoreWithheldReason` (e.g. `no_dilution_snapshot`) means there is NO score — not a score of zero. 🔴 WHEN `levelsAreLowerBound` IS TRUE THE LEVELS ARE FLOORS, NOT MEASUREMENTS: a "medium" then means AT LEAST medium. Name the stated reason, never another. `levelsAreLowerBound` is always present. If a figure is absent, say it was not measured; do not describe the company as having none of that instrument. Figures are as of `meta.asOfDate`, from filings read through `meta.filingsThrough` — a stale as-of date means the answer predates anything filed since, not that nothing has happened. tools.name: get_dilution_instruments
tools.description: Get ONE instrument family's rows with per-field SEC citations — each figure carries the accession number, filing date and the verbatim quoted sentence it was read from, so every number can be traced to a filing. One family per call — request the families you actually need rather than sweeping all ten. 🔴 ROW-LEVEL WITHHOLDING: `withheldRows` / `withheldRowCount` mean specific rows could NOT be verified and were blanked, so every family total in the response is a LOWER BOUND, not a complete figure. Say so — presenting a holed total as complete understates a named issuer's dilution. An empty rows array on a covered company is a measured "none found in the filings read"; an unavailable response is not. 🔴 STATUS `disputed` (warrants / convertibles / preferred / exchangeables) means the ISSUER'S LATEST FILING DISPUTES THE INSTRUMENT'S EXISTENCE OR VALIDITY and its financial statements do not carry it: the row is SHOWN and EXCLUDED from every total (`summary.disputedInstrumentCount` / `disputedInstrumentShares`) — report it as a disputed claim against the company, never as outstanding and never as retired. 🔴 `contingencyTrigger: "event_of_default"` marks an instrument that converts ONLY on an event of default; it is still outstanding and still COUNTED — say "converts only on an event of default", never that it is not dilutive. 🔴 ON `convertibles` ROWS `principalBasis` says HOW `principalOutstanding` was arrived at: `aggregate_only` / `fair_value_only` / `conflict` / `undisclosed_since_issue` mean the current balance is NOT MEASURED (principalOutstanding is null) — report `principalOriginal` as the ORIGINAL principal with the balance undisclosed, never as the current balance. `conversionBasis: "formula_unanchored"` means the conversion mechanism is disclosed but no price input exists, so no share count can be computed — the row is unquantified, not zero. 🔴 ON `convertibles` / `preferred` ROWS `sharesIssuableBasis: "conflict_upper_bound"` means two filed counts DISAGREE and the filings do not explain why: `sharesIssuableIfConverted` is the HIGHER (principal ÷ conversion price, used so dilution is never understated) and `sharesIssuableIssuerStated` is the issuer's own printed figure. Report both, as "up to X; the issuer states Y" — never the higher figure alone as the issuer's count. 🔴 ON `warrants` ROWS a null `sharesUnderlying` beside `aggregateExerciseValueDollars` / `exercisePriceFloor` / `sharesCeilingAsFiled` is a DOLLAR-DENOMINATED or capped warrant: `summary.warrantSharesCeiling` is the MOST such rows could deliver — a ceiling (`≤`), never a count, never in `potentialNewShares`. `warrantCount` is a count of WARRANTS, not shares. 🔴 ON `shelfs` ROWS `babyShelfCurrentCapacityDollars` IS A STORED, DATED FIGURE, NOT TODAY'S HEADROOM: it was struck at extraction time from a float value that may be the issuer's own cover recital months old, less a takedown pool anchored to the corpus window. Always report it WITH its `babyShelfCapacityAsOf` date (`babyShelfCapacityBasis` says which float it rests on); a null date means undated, never current. For the raisable-now figure recomputed from the live float and 60-day-high price call `get_baby_shelf_capacity` — never present the stored figure as current. ALWAYS RETURNS 200 — read `available` and `reason`, never the HTTP status. Coverage is partial: `not_covered` means THIS COMPANY HAS NOT BEEN ANALYSED YET, which is different from it having no dilution and different from an outage (an outage is a 5xx). Never report a company as having no dilution on the strength of an unavailable response. NULL, absent or withheld means NOT MEASURED — it NEVER means "no dilution", "no warrants", "no shelf" or zero. A numeric 0 is a MEASURED zero and defeats a null check, so decide from the accompanying availability/withheld/reason field, never from the value itself. If a figure is absent, say it was not measured; do not describe the company as having none of that instrument. Figures are as of `meta.asOfDate`, from filings read through `meta.filingsThrough` — a stale as-of date means the answer predates anything filed since, not that nothing has happened. Share counts are rebased onto a single split basis; a row that cannot be rebased is omitted and counted rather than published on a mixed basis. tools.name: get_rvol_history
tools.description: Get the per-day relative-volume (RVOL) time series for a ticker, bucketed by trading session (premarket 04:00–09:30 ET, regular 09:30–16:00, afterhours 16:00–20:00, or all four). Each day's RVOL compares that session's volume to a trailing same-session baseline (30 trading days by default — configurable via "baselineDays"), so premarket volume is judged against premarket history (not a stale full-day figure). Use for spotting unusual premarket / session volume surges over the last N days. Each point also carries "baselineState" — "ready" (rvol is populated), "warming" (baseline not yet warm), "no-cutoff-history" (established ticker that never traded at this session/cutoff before) or "no-history" (new listing, no prior trading history at all) — so a null rvol is explained rather than silent. Points additionally carry "advRatio" (that day's volume ÷ the trailing 30-session average FULL-DAY volume, null when no full-day denominator exists) and "advDays" (its sample size), which give a magnitude to points RVOL cannot rate. advRatio is NOT an RVOL — it compares a partial session to a whole day, so it is typically well under 1 and must not be compared to rvol. Charged per your API tier.

session.description: Restrict to one session bucket; omit to return all four sessions.

days.description: Number of trailing calendar days of history (1–90, default 30).

asOfTime.description: Optional TRUE time-of-day premarket basis. Any HH:MM ET premarket time; snapped to the nearest 15-minute grid cutoff (04:00–09:15, ties resolve to the earlier cutoff). When set, the series is the PREMARKET as-of RVOL: cumulative volume known BY that cutoff ÷ the trailing baselineDays (default 30) average of the SAME cutoff (not the full 04:00–09:30 session). Forces the premarket session — any "session" argument is ignored. Each point carries a "basis" field: the snapped cutoff actually used ("asof-0700"), or "full-session" for dates with no precomputed as-of row. Omit for the standard full-session series.

baselineDays.description: Rolling RVOL baseline window, in trading rows (same-session days). Default 30; values outside 20-250 are clamped. This is the DENOMINATOR window: every RVOL in the response is that period's volume divided by the average of the trailing N same-session (or same-cutoff) days, excluding the day itself. A SHORTER window tracks recent regime changes faster and is noisier; a LONGER one is smoother and slower to react. The warm-up lookback scales with it automatically, so a wide window is never under-filled into an inflated ratio; the minimum-warm-days gate (20 prior sessions) does NOT scale down, so at the 30-row default a ticker needs 20 of its last 30 sessions populated before rvol is non-null. Omit for the standard 30-day baseline; pass 90 for the pre-2026-09 window.

tools.name: get_premarket_scanner
tools.description: Get the live premarket scanner board — the top premarket gainers and losers by absolute gap %, each row enriched with rvol, marketCap, floatShares (the measured POINT float, null on a withheld dilution-snapshot row — such a row then carries "floatEstimate" {shares, bound: "point" ~ | "ceiling" <= | "floor" >=, basis}, the snapshot's own labelled figure: present it as the number with its marker, never as a point, never in arithmetic; neither present = not measured, never 0. The low-float board admits on that figure's VALUE: a <= 8M ceiling is in, a >= 26M floor or a ~27M estimate is out), short interest, dilution, and news/catalyst flags. Listing-compliance data (row "compliance", the compliance/split badges, "reverseSplitSignal", "deficiencySignal") is Signal8 Pro: for any other caller "compliance" is null with "complianceWithheld": "pro_required" — WITHHELD, which is not "not measured" and never "no deficiency". Off-hours it falls back to the last session. Use for premarket small-cap runner discovery. Set includePennyStocks=true to include sub-$1 names (separate cache slot). During the 04:00–09:30 ET premarket window rows also carry two LIVE volume metrics off the same live cumulative-volume numerator — they are DIFFERENT quantities and must not be substituted for each other or for "rvol": "liveRvol" = live cumulative premarket volume ÷ the trailing 30-session average cumulative volume AT THE SAME TIME OF MORNING (answers "is it busy for 08:00?"), with "liveRvolAsOf" giving the 15-minute ET grid cutoff that baseline came from — compare it to meta.asOf (when the live volume was sampled) to judge the small numerator/denominator time skew; and "premarketPaceRatio" = the same live volume ÷ the trailing 30-session average FULL premarket session (answers "what fraction of a typical entire premarket has it already done?", >1.0 = it already beat a normal premarket before the open). Both are null outside the premarket window or until the baseline is warm — never a fabricated ratio. Set universe="lowfloat" for the separate LOW-FLOAT board (float under 10M shares, no top-100 slice) instead of the default movers-derived board; that board is served from the aggregator snapshot and returns an empty rows array with a meta.reason when no snapshot is currently published (a normal off-hours state, not an error). Charged per your API tier.

includePennyStocks.description: Include sub-$1 (penny) stocks in the results. Default false.

universe.description: Which board to return. "default" (the default) is the movers-derived top-100 board. "lowfloat" is the low-float board (float < 10M shares, no top-100 slice).

sort.description: Sort key for the low-float board: "gap" (default) or "rvol". Ignored for universe="default", which is always gap-ranked.

tools.name: get_upcoming_reverse_splits
tools.description: Get reverse stock splits SCHEDULED to take effect within a day-offset window of the current US market day, for companies under a market-cap ceiling. Offsets are days from today on the US market calendar: fromOffset=1, toOffset=1 is tomorrow; fromOffset=1, toOffset=7 is the week ahead. Each row carries the ticker, company name, the exact vendor integers (splitFrom/splitTo), a pre-rendered ratio ("1-for-20"), the effective date, market cap, float in SHARES, and price. 🔴 floatShares: null MEANS NOT MEASURED OR WITHHELD — never zero, never "no float". Such rows ARE included (they have a valid market cap); floatWithheldReason says why. Do not substitute a float from another source. floatUnknownCount counts those null-float rows IN the list; it is not a withholding count (withheldCount is). price is on the SAME split basis as the market cap (null when it cannot be stated on one basis), so never pair it with a pre-split price from elsewhere. WHAT THIS IS: rows are splits scheduled AS OF NOW — not a guarantee that every split effective in the window is already known. The underlying stock_splits table has NO created_at column, so there is no way to measure when a row first appeared, and a split announced later will simply be missing. Describe results as "scheduled as of now", NEVER as "all of" or "every" reverse split. A scheduled split can also be postponed or cancelled after it is announced. 🔴 capUnknownCount IS A WITHHOLDING COUNT, NOT A ZERO. It counts rows that passed every other filter and were DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED because Signal8 has no measured market cap for them — typically real OTC microcaps. It does NOT mean those companies have no dilution, no split, or no cap; it means the cap was not measured, so they cannot be asserted to sit under the stated ceiling. If you publish a "under $Xm" framing and capUnknownCount is above zero, say that N further companies were withheld for unmeasured market cap — do not present the list as complete and do not describe the withheld rows at all. Funds, ETFs and sub-1.5x fractional ratio adjustments are already removed server-side; do not re-filter or re-derive the ratio. AN EMPTY splits ARRAY IS A NORMAL, COMMON RESULT — most single weekdays have no sub-cap reverse split scheduled at all. It is NOT an error, NOT a failure, and NOT evidence that reverse-split activity has stopped. Publish nothing rather than publishing an empty-list framing.

fromOffset.description: Window start as a day offset from the US market day (default 1 = tomorrow). Must be <= toOffset; an inverted window is rejected rather than silently returning an empty list.

toOffset.description: Window end, inclusive, as a day offset from the US market day (default 1). Use 7 with fromOffset 1 for the week ahead.

maxMarketCap.description: Exclusive market-cap ceiling in USD (default 300000000). Rows with NO measured market cap are excluded and counted in capUnknownCount, never assumed to be under the ceiling.

tools.name: get_recent_uplistings
tools.description: Get OTC-to-exchange uplistings that FINRA recorded on a given US market day, for companies under a market-cap ceiling. Each row carries the old OTC symbol, the resolved new exchange symbol (or null), a confirmed flag, the destination venue (NASDAQ / NYSE / NYSE American / ARCA), company name, effective date, market cap and float in SHARES. 🔴 THIS IS A SAME-DAY READ AND THERE IS NO FORWARD-LOOKING VERSION. FINRA records an uplisting at roughly 01:45 ET ON the day it becomes effective, and the source table has no scheduled/announced column at all. So there is nothing to publish the night before, and dayOffset exists for catch-up reads of past days, NOT for forecasting — a positive offset returns nothing. Never frame these as upcoming, tomorrow, or expected; they have already happened. 🔴 newSymbol: null IS A FIRST-CLASS PUBLISHED STATE, NOT A MISSING FIELD. FINRA's row names only the OLD OTC symbol; the new ticker is resolved by company-name match against Nasdaq SymDir and sometimes cannot be resolved. A guessed or wrong ticker would name a company that did not uplist, so an unresolved row is published naming the OLD symbol and saying the new one was not resolved. DO NOT infer, guess, look up, or fill in a null newSymbol, and do not drop the row. confirmed: false means the symbol resolution is PROVISIONAL — render it as provisional, keep it out of any headline, and do not assert the new ticker as fact. Only confirmed: true is a confirmed resolution. 🔴 capUnknownCount IS A WITHHOLDING COUNT, NOT A ZERO — rows that cleared every other filter but have NO measured market cap, so they cannot be asserted to sit under the stated ceiling. It does not mean those companies have no cap. Disclose the count if you publish a cap-bracketed framing. AN EMPTY uplistings ARRAY IS THE NORMAL, EXPECTED RESULT ON MOST DAYS — uplistings run roughly 6.6 per month across ALL market caps, so the large majority of days genuinely have none. It is NOT an error, NOT an outage, and NOT evidence that uplisting activity has stopped. Publish nothing rather than publishing an empty-list framing.

dayOffset.description: Day offset from the US market day (default 0 = today). Negative values read past days. A positive value returns nothing — there is no forward-looking uplisting data.

maxMarketCap.description: Exclusive market-cap ceiling in USD (default 300000000). Rows with NO measured market cap are excluded and counted in capUnknownCount, never assumed to be under the ceiling.

tools.name: search_learn_guides
tools.description: Search the free Signal8 Academy (signal8.ai/learn) — plain-English guides that explain dilution (ATMs, warrants, convertibles, baby shelf, cash runway), how to read SEC filings (8-K items, Form 4 codes, 13D/13G, 424B5, S-1/S-3), market structure (halts, short interest, float, reverse splits, STOCK Act disclosures) and how to use Signal8. Returns matching guides with title, description, track, section, reading time, lastVerified date, the public url and the signal8:// resource uri — no bodies; call get_learn_guide for the full Markdown. Keyword match: every query word must appear somewhere in the guide; title hits rank highest. An empty query lists every guide (optionally one track) in reading order. Use this to ground an explanation of a concept the user asked about, or to cite a guide alongside data from the dilution / filing tools. Works without an API key. An empty result means no guide matched the words given — try fewer or broader words (e.g. "warrant" rather than "warrant inducement repricing") — not that the topic is unimportant.

query.description: Words to search for, e.g. "baby shelf", "form 4", "reverse split". Empty string lists every guide.

track.description: Optional. Restrict to one Academy track: "dilution" (dilution & toxic financing), "filings" (reading SEC filings), "market-structure" (halts, short interest, float, splits, congressional trading), or "signal8" (using Signal8, its API and this MCP server).

tools.name: get_learn_guide
tools.description: Get one Signal8 Academy guide as Markdown, by track and slug (both come from search_learn_guides, or from a signal8.ai/learn/<track>/<slug> URL). Returns title, description, section, lastVerified, the public url, the full Markdown body (links already rewritten to absolute signal8.ai URLs), the related guides, the glossary terms it uses (with one-line definitions) and its SEC sources (accession numbers). Guides use hypothetical examples ("Company X") unless a source is cited; they are education, not advice about any named company. When you quote or paraphrase a guide, cite its url. Works without an API key.

track.description: Academy track: "dilution" (dilution & toxic financing), "filings" (reading SEC filings), "market-structure" (halts, short interest, float, splits, congressional trading), or "signal8" (using Signal8, its API and this MCP server).

tools.name: define_term
tools.description: Look up a term in the Signal8 Academy glossary (signal8.ai/learn/glossary) — dilution, SEC filing and trading jargon such as "ATM offering", "baby shelf", "full ratchet", "pre-funded warrant", "going concern", "LULD", "days to cover", "Form 25". Accepts a glossary slug ("atm-offering"), the term itself, or a common alias ("ATM", "price reset"); matching is case- and punctuation-insensitive. Returns the term, a one-line short definition, the long definition as Markdown, related terms, the Academy guides that use it, and the public url. A TERM_NOT_FOUND error means the glossary has no entry for that wording — not that the concept does not exist; try search_learn_guides with the same words. Works without an API key.

term.description: Term, alias or glossary slug, e.g. "baby shelf", "ATM", "full-ratchet".

instructions:
Signal8 provides read-only SEC-filing intelligence and market data for US-listed companies, plus US congressional & executive-branch (STOCK Act) trading and FEC campaign-finance data.

Typical workflow:
- Resolve a company first with `search_companies` (name or ticker), then call company tools — `get_company_profile`, `get_quote`, `get_financials`, `get_short_interest`, `get_float`, `get_earnings`, insider trades (`get_insiders`), and institutional/total ownership (`get_institutions`, `get_ownership`). Most tools take a bare ticker (e.g. "AAPL").
- For SEC filing text/exhibits, use the EDGAR tools (`search_sec_filings`, `get_filing_document`).
- For small-cap dilution (warrants, convertibles, preferred, shelf registrations, ATMs, equity lines, baby-shelf capacity, cash runway) call `get_dilution_coverage` first, then `get_dilution_risk`, `get_dilution_snapshot` and `get_dilution_instruments` (one family per call); `get_baby_shelf_capacity`, `get_dilution_performance` and `get_dilution_history` cover the rest. Every figure is cited to its SEC filing. A null, withheld or unavailable figure means NOT MEASURED, never "no dilution". The `explain_dilution` prompt runs the whole workflow.
- For political trading use the politician tools (`get_politicians`, `get_politician_transactions`, `get_senate_trades_by_ticker`); for campaign finance use the donor tools.
- To explain a concept (dilution instruments, SEC forms, halts, float, reverse splits) or define jargon, use the free Signal8 Academy tools (`search_learn_guides`, `get_learn_guide`, `define_term`) and cite the guide URL. They work without an API key.

Prefer lightweight lookups (`get_company_profile`, `get_quote`) before the heavier `get_company_bundle`. Calls are metered by the caller's API-key tier, so batch intent into the most specific tool rather than many broad calls.
